compound_ladder.label: calibrated (0.21% of lap time)
compound_ladder.derivation: fresh-tyre step prior 0.178 s (calibrated (0.21% of lap time)). The races identify the *net* cost of one step harder over a whole stint, holding stint length and race phase fixed: australia-2026 +0.317 +/- 0.345 s; japan-2026 -0.069 +/- 0.664 s; barcelona-2026 +0.060 +/- 0.336 s; austria-2026 +0.106 +/- 0.295 s; belgium-2026 +0.075 +/- 0.323 s; hungary-2026 -0.010 +/- 0.327 s; italy-2026 +0.173 +/- 0.354 s -> pooled +0.108 +/- 0.131 s per step. The model's fresh-tyre offsets are calibrated so that, with its own degradation ladder, it reproduces this net at the stint length it recommends.

regime.label: median of 7 donors, temperature-corrected
regime.derivation: race/practice degradation ratio, stint-fixed-effects estimator on both sessions; each donor's log ratio corrected by the thermal sensitivity (+0.025/degC) times its race-minus-practice track temperature, residuals pooled with the median: australia-2026 0.75x (dT +2 degC -> 0.72), japan-2026 0.73x (dT +2 degC -> 0.70), barcelona-2026 0.70x (dT +2 degC -> 0.66), austria-2026 0.58x (dT +2 degC -> 0.56), belgium-2026 0.32x (dT -5 degC -> 0.37), hungary-2026 0.64x (dT +17 degC -> 0.42), italy-2026 0.81x (dT +2 degC -> 0.78) -> management residual 0.66x (spread 0.24 ln); at spain-2026 practice ran at 50 degC and the race is expected at 53 degC (forecast supplied), so the pool gives 0.71x, so 0.71x applies; the old pooled geometric mean would have given 0.63x. spain-2026's own race is never used

pace_offset_s.note: the level of the car's clean long-run laps against the field's own compound/age trend; negative is quicker than the field.  It is confounded by the run programme - practice long runs differ in fuel load and in how hard they are being driven, and neither is observable here - so it is reported, not charged: no cost in the objective reads it (see car_terms)

deg_rate_by_compound.note: the field rate plus the fit's own dev[d, c], pooled driver -> team by percar.team_pooled_dev at k = 20 clean laps; the team -> field step is the fit's own hierarchical pull on dev (sigma_dev ~ HalfNormal(0.02)) and is not applied twice here

age_sensitivity.note: the same pooled deviation as one number: how much more lap time per lap of tyre age this car gives away than the field

warmup_s.note: mean excess of laps 1/2 of a stint over that stint's own trend (fitted from lap 3); in a practice table lap 1 is the out-lap and is filtered out, so this is normally the first flying lap.  A pool of fewer than 2 stints contributes nothing

consistency_s.note: residual SD about the stint trend, over the laps the trend was fitted on

traffic_sensitivity.note: the car's excess over the stint trend within 2 s of the car ahead, divided by the field's same excess (0.389 s/lap over 22 laps); 1.0 is a car that loses what everyone loses; this car's 2 in-traffic lap(s) are below the 3-lap floor and contribute nothing

push_response.note: not identifiable pre-race: a practice long run is a full-push experiment by construction, so this weekend carries no within-car variation in push from which a per-car management response could be estimated.  The calibrated team/field value is used, fully shrunk

sector_deg.note: per-sector slope against tyre age over this car's long runs, from the FastF1 cache's sector times

pace_vs_teammate_s.note: this car's level minus BEA's, shrunk toward 0 (the two cars are the same car) by the thinner of the two samples

terms.note: warmup_s and traffic_mult are field-relative: a car with no evidence gets the calibrated field values unchanged

explanation: OCO: 1-stop M-H @ 30; BEA: 1-stop M-H @ 30 - the same first stop (lap 30); the same plan shape
S1 degradation: OCO +0.0360 vs BEA -0.0027 s/lap of age (+0.0387); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=7, w=0.37, team | BEA: n=7, w=0.37, team]

pace level: OCO 0.738 s/lap vs BEA 0.377 s/lap (+0.362); the quicker car reaches any given gap to the car ahead sooner, which moves the lap its stop is worth taking [OCO: n=5, w=0.38, team | BEA: n=6, w=0.43, team]
S2 degradation: OCO -0.0112 vs BEA +0.0190 s/lap of age (-0.0301); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=7, w=0.37, team | BEA: n=7, w=0.37, team]

race-history rate factor (from previous races, not this weekend's evidence): OCO x1.070 vs BEA x1.189 after precision shrinkage (raw x1.115 / x1.318, ln_sd 0.07795004439288562 / 0.07723749666602743); it scales the whole rate, so the higher factor stops earlier
S3 degradation: OCO +0.0836 vs BEA +0.0897 s/lap of age (-0.0061); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=7, w=0.37, team | BEA: n=7, w=0.37, team]
the two recommendations agree: the differences above are not big enough to separate the plans
